lesson.title: Have You Earned the Net?
lesson.hook: A short ball invites you forward. Read your arrival before committing to the next shot.
lesson.memHTML: Arrive first. Then decide whether to follow.
lesson.tomorrow: On a short ball, read your arrival and their position together. From a controlled position, an approach may fit. If you are still chasing, prioritise a manageable reply before committing forward.
lesson.cue: Arrive first. Then decide whether to follow.

pro.label: Borges · The secret was when, not just how
pro.moment: Asked about his successful net play, Nuno Borges put the emphasis on selection: “I just chose really wisely when to come in.” He had been working on the approach and the moment to use it. His net game began with choosing which balls deserved the trip forward.
pro.read: Your next point: read your arrival and the ball. A purposeful approach can earn a manageable volley; chasing a low ball gives you a different job.
pro.src: Nuno Borges · ATP interview on his 2025 net play · January 2026

steps.name: Choose your plan
steps.sit: Their reply lands inside the service line. They remain deep.
opts: Lift a deep approach and follow it in
Lift deep, regain position before committing
steps.payoff: Controlled arrival and a deep opponent can support an approach.
steps.principle: Read your arrival as well as the ball and the opponent.
steps.why: You are prepared inside the court and the opponent is still deep. Lift the low ball with margin and follow a purposeful approach. Getting to the net is a plan, not a promise of an easy volley.
steps.take: Controlled arrival and a deep opponent can support an approach.

lines.A: Lift with depth; the controlled arrival supports following it in.
lines.B: A reset is possible, but you can use this forward position.

steps.name: Choose your plan
steps.sit: The same short ball. They are still deep. Watch your arrival.
opts: Lift a deep approach and follow it in
Lift deep, regain position before committing
steps.payoff: Reaching a short ball does not automatically earn the net.
steps.principle: Read your arrival as well as the ball and the opponent.
steps.why: This time you started farther away and are still chasing forward. Prioritise a reply you can control. Judge whether to keep coming from the quality of that shot, rather than committing to the net before you have made it.
steps.take: Reaching a short ball does not automatically earn the net.

lines.A: Committing now asks too much of an arrival still in progress.
lines.B: Make a manageable reply, then judge the next position.

steps.name: Choose your plan
steps.sit: A new point on the other wing. Choose your plan.
opts: Drive flat for the open corner
Lift a deep approach and follow it in
steps.payoff: Being prepared does not remove the need to read the ball.
steps.principle: Read your arrival as well as the ball and the opponent.
steps.why: You have arrived, but the backhand contact will be low. Preparation makes a controlled approach available; it does not make a flat finish from below net height the better plan. Use lift and margin against the deep opponent.
steps.take: Being prepared does not remove the need to read the ball.

lines.A: Your arrival is good, but the low ball still needs lift.
lines.B: Prepared, low ball, opponent deep: lift the approach with margin.

drill.name: Call the plan
drill.how: With a partner, vary the feed and your starting position. Before contact, call “pressure” or “buy time”. Afterwards, compare the call with your arrival, the ball and their position. Keep a useful cue; a won or lost point alone does not settle the decision.

readiness.evidence: Prepared inside the court; opponent still deep.
Still chasing forward as the ball arrives.
Prepared on the backhand; low ball, opponent deep.
